I have been following the UK singles Chart since 1980 in one form or another. It's absolutely stupid, ridiculous, idiotic and absurd that Sam Fender & Olivia Dean's "Rein In Me" has been #1 on the singles chart for 20 weeks, for 5 months alltogether!!!

The entire Official Singles Chart has completely lost its value. It's become nothing more than one huge joke!

Including streaming in the chart calculations was a terrible decision. The only chart that really reflects actual single purchases is The Singles Sales Chart.

To be honest, I can hardly even be bothered to listen to the Official Singles Chart anymore. The same songs just stay on the chart for months and months!

Absolutely ridiculous!!

Pekka (Peter) from Finland

drupalComments.title: 00d5a2d2-0b5f-45ca-a3b1-690ede5d607e
drupalComments.body:
It is very disheartening to hear and read all the negativity surrounding the achievement of Sam Fender and Olivia Dean on overtaking Frankie Lane as having the most non-consecutive weeks at Number One in the UK. Surely, we should be celebrating the success of British artists attaining such an accomplishment, not knocking them? Why does a portion of our society delight in being belligerent to anyone who attains even a modicum of success?

As a Charts Aficionado since the mid-sixties, when Alan Freeman’s Pick of the Pops was The Show to listen to every Sunday, I quickly grew to appreciate that all genre of music has a place, and an equal right to be heard. That was when the Top Forty had true diversity – Rock, Tamla, Northern Soul, R&B, Reggae, Dance, Country, a heady mix of male and female solo artists, and good old “pop” music. I believe the jury is still out as to whether today’s “Charts” contain as much miscellany.

Sadly, we live in an all-too-frequently disagreeable digital age; one where it is far easier to ridicule, insult, and be darn-right offensive with impunity, rather than learning to respect the fact that we all have the right and freedom to enjoy our own musical journey, without censure.

To quote John Lennon: “Music is everybody’s possession”.

For the correct information as to how the UK Singles Charts are devised, visit: https://www.officialcharts.com/getting-into-the-charts/how-the-charts-are-compiled/

drupalComments.title: aabff97b-32a8-400d-b0df-b78b1cba184a
drupalComments.body: Hmmm - a lot of anger about in the comments. Let's just say these few bits. There have always been re-released songs charting 10 or 20 years after their first release, so the charts have never been totally about brand new music. There have been numerous novelty and not so great records getting to #1. Then, records that are genuinely regarded as great or classic do not always reach #1 - some don't even chart at all.  Records in sport, music, whatever - were always set to be broken. I am celebrating 'Rein Me In' as our new all-time longest UK #1, replacing the great Frankie Laine 'I Believe'. Musical taste is very personal, but I think 'Rein Me In' is a very special track, and worthier than Bryan Adams or Wet Wet Wet alternatives, which were both propelled by massive films. Nice one, Sam & Olivia. We will be seeing this track in those frequent listener-compiled all-time top 500 charts done by many commercial radio stations, and it will deserve to be there.

drupalComments.body:
I was rooting for ‘Dai Dai’ to hold on so that we could at least have something fresh at the top, but unfortunately not.

Look, I like ‘Rein Me In’, but I really don’t understand its appeal to the point where it’s now the longest #1 single in history. I’d even argue that both Sam and Olivia have better songs than this. 

The irony is that ACR was introduced to rotate old songs out faster, yet if you removed it, this would "only" be its 15th week there and Frankie Laine would still have the record. 

Congratulations to them, although now that it’s got there, I seriously hope that Ariana can knock it off the summit next week for good.
